fields.statement: Which intent should change set 'The daemon holds new runs' (CPU load and memory hold) serve? I recommend m4-orchestrated-by-rhiza: hand-tuning maxRuns is orchestrator work the daemon should do itself. / How should the load hold trigger and release? I recommend: hold when the 1-minute load per core is over rhiza.daemon.maxLoad (default 3.0); release only once the 5-minute load per core is back under it. Memory: hold while MemAvailable is under rhiza.daemon.minMemory (default 2G), release once it is back at or over it. / Where unsupported, how is load/memory read? I recommend: Linux reads /proc/loadavg and MemAvailable; macOS reads load via sysctl vm.loadavg and skips the memory check; other platforms skip both, and daemon status says the reading is unavailable. / When does a load/memory hold reach rhiza health and the inbox? I recommend after it has lasted 30 minutes (a fixed threshold, no setting); daemon status and the daemon log show every hold and release at once.
